summary: The note celebrates the resurgence of wood-fired oven cooking since September 1, 2023, covering how the ovens work, the wood choices that shape flavor, and profiles of chefs, home cooks and an artist who use them. It also highlights communal events, pizza craft, seasonal produce and the sustainability case for wood-fired baking. The overall theme is a living link between tradition and innovation.
one_line: A tour of the wood-fired oven revival through bakers, pizzaiolos, community events, an artist and sustainability arguments.
key_facts: Since September 1, 2023, a resurgence in traditional cooking methods has put the wood-fired oven back in the culinary spotlight.
Chef Marco Tulio, a third-generation baker, opened his artisanal bakery 'Flame & Dough' in Vermont on October 12, 2023.
Wood-fired ovens have an inner dome traditionally made of refractory bricks or clay that absorbs fire heat and radiates it evenly, while a dense stone floor stores heat for a crisp base.

Avi Patel, a self-taught cooking enthusiast from Asheville, began wood-fired baking in early spring 2024 and built a backyard oven from a kit and locally sourced materials; her first pizza was a margherita cooked with applewood.
On November 8, 2023, at the 'Taste of Fire' festival in Texas, Chef Kathy Leung prepared a full menu, from smoked brisket to roasted vegetables, in her mobile wood-fired oven.
Mesquite gives a bold, smoky flavor while alder gives a more subtle note.
Tulio says wood-fired baking requires learning to 'read the fire' and understand the hot spots within the dome, unlike precise modern oven controls.
On September 19, 2023, Cedar Ridge, Oregon, held its annual 'Harvest Dinner' around a communal wood-fired oven.
At 'Flame & Dough', customers are invited each morning to tear into fresh sourdough loaves made with a long fermentation.
Lorenzo Rossi, a pizzaiolo from Naples, cooks pizzas with fresh mozzarella, San Marzano tomatoes and basil, retrieving them after 90 seconds; the visit described was December 1, 2023.
The 'Autumn Flavors' event on October 5, 2023 used wood-fired ovens to turn squash, root vegetables and hearty herbs into caramelized, smoke-kissed dishes.
Emily Grant has shown ceramics fired in her wood-fired oven at the 'Heat & Harvest' art installation in Portland since September 2023.
A conference on sustainable cooking techniques on Earth Day, April 22, 2024, discussed the carbon-neutral potential of responsibly sourced wood and the benefits of communal ovens.
